flashcard_questions.a: A style that repeats small musical ideas over a long time.
A short musical pattern that repeats continuously.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a loop or cell?
flashcard_questions.a: A repeating idea that comes and goes rather than playing continuously.

flashcard_questions.q: What is layering in minimalist music?
flashcard_questions.a: Adding new parts gradually so the texture thickens.

flashcard_questions.q: What is subtraction in minimalist music?
flashcard_questions.a: Removing parts gradually so the texture thins.
Two parts play the same pattern while one drifts out of sync.
Harmony that stays on one chord, or changes very little.

flashcard_questions.q: What effect does a thin-to-thick texture create?
flashcard_questions.a: A sense of something building or approaching.

flashcard_questions.q: What effect does a thick-to-thin texture create?
flashcard_questions.a: A feeling of isolation or emptiness.

flashcard_questions.q: Which composer wrote the score for Arrival?
In which year was the film Arrival released?
What is repeated throughout Heptapod B?
Which composer wrote the score for Interstellar?
Which kind of ostinato drives Mountains from Interstellar?
What does each tick of the ostinato in Mountains represent?

notes: 15 cards: 7 technique term-to-definition cards (minimalism, ostinato, loop or cell, layering, subtraction, phase shifting, static harmony), 2 texture-to-effect cards, and 6 example-to-feature cards on the two named cues (Arrival's composer and year, the repeated phrase in Heptapod B, Interstellar's composer, the ticking ostinato and what each tick represents). Each card names the cue itself, so no card depends on the one before it.
